 JUDGMENT

The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident dated 26.06.2023.
2.

The case of the Petitioner in brief is that, On 26.06.2023 at about 16.00hours the petitioner was riding his Hero Honda Two Wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA-06-EH- 8733 on the left side of SH-84 Road towards Yadeyuru, slowly observing all the traffic rules.

When he reached near SCCH - 25 3 MVC No. 5791/2023 Doddamadhure Govt. High School, Yedeyuru Hobli, Kunigal Taluk, Tumakuru Dist., Ashok Leyland Goods Vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-06-AA-2795 came with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life, all of a sudden came to its wrong/right side of the Road from Yedeyuru side i.e., from opposite direction and dashed to the petitioner's motorcycle.
Due to impact he fell down and suffered injuries.

sentences.text:
3. It is the further case of the petitioner that, immediately after the accident he was shifted to Adichunchanagiri Hospital, B.G.Nagar, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient, underwent operations of CRIF with long PEN from femur, ORIF with CC screw for lateral condyle of femur,
ORIF with CC screw fixation for proximal tibia fracture right side under general anesthesia, below slab for left sided distal end radius fracture and got discharged on 30.06.2023.

Due to severe pain in the fracture, again the petitioner was admitted to the same hospital as an inpatient on 01.07.2023,
underwent CRIF with K-wire and ORIF with plating for distal end radius fracture under supra clavicular SCCH - 25 4 MVC No. 5791/2023 block and discharged on 20.07.2023 with an advice for complete bed rest.
So far he has spent Rs.1,85,000/- towards hospitalization and medicines.
Prior to the date of accident he was hale and healthy, doing Agriculture and Milk Vending and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to the accident he could not work and he could not do his day today activities also and lost all his income.
The accident is due to the sole negligence of the driver of the Ashok Leyland Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-06-AA-2795.

The jurisdictional Amruthur police have registered a case against the driver of the offending vehicle in Cr.No.0100/2023 p/u/Sec.279,
337 & 338 of IPC.
Therefore, the 1st respondent being the RC owner and the 2 nd respondent being the insurer of the said offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to him.
Hence, this petition.
4. In response to notice issued by this Tribunal, the Respondents appeared and filed separate written statements.

The objection of the respondent No.1.
SCCH - 25 5 MVC No. 5791/2023

He has denied all the petition averments except admitting that the 2nd respondent insurer had issued a Policy covering the risk of the Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-06-AA-2795 belonging to this respondent bearing policy No.VB555968 valid from 12.04.2023 to 11.04.2024 and the said policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further stated that The 2 nd respondent being the insurer of the vehicle belonging to this respondent is liable to pay the compensation.
He has denied the manner of accident.
Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
Therefore prayed for dismissal of the petition.
6. The objection of the respondent No.2.

It has denied all the averments of the petition except admitting the issuance of policy in favour fo the 1 st respondent in respect of the Asok Leyland Dost Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-06-AA-2795.
There is non compliance of Sec.134(c) of MV Act.
Further contended that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess a valid DL and a valid RC to the vehicle as on the date of accident.
It has also denied the age, SCCH - 25 6 MVC No. 5791/2023 occupation and the manner of accident.

It contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive,
arbitrary and disproportionate.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against it.

1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that, the accident occurred on 26.06.2023 at 04.00pm, due to rash and negligent driving by the diver of Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-06-AA-2795 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3.
What order or award?

Dr.Nagaraj B.N. got examined as PW.3 and got marked SCCH - 25 7 MVC No. 5791/2023 Exs.P.17 & 18.
On the other side, the Respondents did not examine any witness nor produced any documents on their behalf.

10.

On hearing both sides and perusal of the evidence on record this court answers the above issues as follows:-

17.

From the evidence of PW.3 and the documents on record, it is clear that the petitioner has suffered right sub- trochanteric fracture and shaft fracture, lateral condyle fracture of the right femur, proximal tibia, fracture and left distal radius fracture with lacerated wound over the left foot and undergone surgeries with CRIF with long PEN for the right femur, CC Screw for the lateral condyle of the femur, ORIF with CC Screw for the right proximal tibia and also got ORIF for right distal radius fracture.
So it will be difficult for him to do the work.

This kind of disability will affect his day to day work.

sentences.text: The Petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, he was an Agriculture and doing Milk Vending and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
In this regard he has not examined any witness nor produced any documents like Bank statement etc., to prove his earnings.
The accident occurred in the year 2023.
Therefore, this court deems it fit to fix the notional income at Rs.16,000/- per month.

At the time of accident the Petitioner was aged about 39 years as could be made out from Exs.P.9 &
10/Notarized copy of Aadhar Card & PAN Card.
He was hale and healthy before the accident.

Keeping all the above things in mind, Petitioner is entitled to the following compensation:-
 i) PAIN AND SUFFERING:-

After the accident, the Petitioner was treated at Adichunchangiri Hospital wherein he was admitted and treated as an inpatient from 26.06.2023 to 30.06.2023 and from 01.07.2023 to 20.07.2023 was diagnosed and underwent surgery which can be made out from Ex.P.8 Discharge SCCH - 25 14 MVC No. 5791/2023 summaries of the said hospital.
Considering that the nature of injuries he has undergone are grievous and simple, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- under this head.
ii) MEDICAL EXPENSES:

The Petitioner has pleaded that he has spent huge amount towards treatment, medicines,
conveyance, food and nourishment and other incidental expenses etc.
In this regard, he has produced medical bills as per Ex.P.11 for a sum of Rs.63,109/- There is no contrary evidence against these bills from the Respondents.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for the above said amount under this head.

iii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:-
As mentioned above the petitioner has sustained grievous and simple injuries.
The petitioner has produced discharge summaries of Aadichunchanagiri Hospital to show the duration and treatment in the said hospital.

Therefore, considering the nature of injuries it can be said that the Petitioner may have required at least Three months time for SCCH - 25 15 MVC No. 5791/2023 recovering from the injuries sustained by him.
Hence, he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.48,000/- under this head.

iv) LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME:-
On perusal of Ex.P.9/Notarized copy of Aadhar Card, the date of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 01.01.1984.
the accident occurred on 26.06.2023.
Therefore, as on the date of the accident the Petitioner's age is 39 years.
As per the dictum laid down in Sarala Verma's case the appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 15.

Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.7,20,000/- (Rs.16,000/-
x 12 x 15 x 25%= Rs.7,20,000/-) under this head.

(v) LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND Gopinatha vs Karthik L on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176911787/
6  HAPPINESS:-

sentences.text: The Petitioner was aged about 39 years at the time of accident.
He has sustained grievous and simple injuries and as per consideration of this Tribunal, he is suffering from 25% functional disability.
The Petitioner has to suffer this disability throughout his life.
Because of this he will have to lose some of SCCH - 25 16 MVC No. 5791/2023 the amenities and comforts.
Therefore, considering the age and nature of injuries that the Petitioner has suffered, a sum of Rs.20,000/- is awarded under this head.
(vi) ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT CHARGES:
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated in the above said hospital, admitted as an inpatient and discharged with advise.
However, during this period he must have spent considerable amount on his food and nourishment, conveyance and attendant expenses.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.
(vii) FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
As per the version of PW.3, the Petitioner has to undergo another surgery for removal of implant and the estimate of this surgery is around Rs.60,000/-.
In this regard the petitioner or PW.3 has not issued the estimation letter.

Therefore, looking at the earlier treatment cost and nature of injury and the evidence on record, it appears it would be SCCH - 25 17 MVC No. 5791/2023 justifiable if an amount of Rs.20,000/- is awarded to the Petitioner under this head.
Therefore, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.

19. The Petitioner is entitled to compensation under the following heads:
1. Pain & suffering Rs.1,00,000/-
2. Medical expenses Rs.63,109/-
3. Loss of income during laid up Rs.48,000/- period 4. Loss of future income Rs.7,20,000/-
5. Loss of future amenities and Rs.20,000/- happiness 6. Attendant, conveyance, food and Rs.20,000/- nourishment charges 7.

Future Medical Expenses Rs.20,000/-
TOTAL Rs.9,91,109/-

Liability 20.
The Respondent No.2 did not prove its defence.

Therefore, the Respondents being the RC owner and the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable SCCH - 25 18 MVC No.
5791/2023 to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
However, as the policy existed as on the date of accident, the respondent No.2/insurer has to indemnify the respondent No.1/insured and has to pay compensation awarded to the petitioner.

The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.30,00,000/-
but he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.9,91,200/- with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed.
Accordingly, Issue No.3 is held in the affirmative.
21. Issue No.4:-

For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.9,91,200/- (Rupees Nine Lakhs Ninety One Thousand and Two Hundred only) along with interest at 6% p.a. (Except future medical SCCH - 25 19 MVC No. 5791/2023 expenses) from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation to the petitioner.
However, the Respondent No.2/Insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within sixty days from the date of this award.

On deposit of compensation and interest, 25% shall be deposited in the name of the petitioner for a period of 3 years in any Bank and remaining amount shall be released in favour of the Petitioner by way of e-payment on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per rules.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw decree accordingly.
